summary:
Baja California operates an administrative procedure for legal gender recognition. The state congress created it through a 2022 reform to the Civil Code, initially limited to adults. In June 2023 Mexico's Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation struck down the law's adults-only requirement, holding that it failed to recognise the rights of transgender children and adolescents. In 2024 the state congress passed a further reform establishing a procedure for people under 18 and extending legal gender recognition to non-binary people. Legal gender recognition is a matter of state competence within Mexico's federal system.

Lethal violence against women in the state is documented as under-typified, and a serial feminicide case in Tijuana's tolerance zone bears on the enforcement record. Zeta Tijuana reported on 8 July 2023 that Brayan Rivera was accused by Mexico of the feminicide of Ángela Carolina Acosta, killed on 24 January 2022 in room 404 of Hotel Cascadas beside Bar Hong Kong in Tijuana's tolerance zone. He was arrested at his parents' home in Downey, California, where officers found a Hotel Cascadas rent receipt, rope and gloves. The Baja California attorney general called the 30-year-old a serial perpetrator, said extradition could take from 15 days to two years, and said nearly a decade of open case files were being reviewed; the investigation had linked him to at least three feminicides: Ángela (January 2022), Elizabeth (14 February), and Karen, 28 (30 August 2021, Motel Hacienda Soler). The source identifies the victims as women and does not state that any was transgender.
tangentialFactors:
The case has a cross-border procedural dimension. Brayan Rivera was presented on 6 July 2023 before US Judge Karen L. Stevenson in provisional detention for extradition, and probable cause was determined on 29 June 2023 by the US federal court.

For comparison, Mexico City criminalised transfemicide on 18 July 2024 under the Paola Buenrostro law, with sentences of up to 70 years; the inventory records no equivalent offence in Baja California. Nationally, over 95% of homicides went unpunished in 2022.
localsOnly: Under Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila, 1,179 women have been killed in Baja California while only 110 cases were typified as feminicide, a share that indicates under-classification of lethal violence against women in the state (Zeta Tijuana, 8 March 2025).
outOfScopeNotes: The inventory does not record whether Baja California's criminal code contains hate-motivation provisions or a transfemicide offence, nor how the state's gender recognition procedure performs in practice. The outcome of the extradition proceedings against Brayan Rivera is not recorded. The Tijuana feminicide victims are identified in the source as women; the source does not state that any was transgender, so the case cannot be presented as a trans-specific killing.
